nameStory: The 'pearly' in this moth's name comes from the lustrous, iridescent sheen on its wings that catches light like mother-of-pearl. The 'wood-nymph' part refers to its forest habitat and the delicate, fairy-like appearance of this graceful moth as it flutters through woodland clearings.
description: The Pearly Wood-nymph is a medium-sized moth with a wingspan of about 1 to 1.4 inches across. It belongs to the cutworm moth family, though unlike many of its drab relatives, this species displays beautiful pearlescent wings with intricate patterns. Adults are active during the warmer months and are often attracted to lights at night. Despite being called a 'wood-nymph,' these moths can be found in various habitats where their host plants grow.

idTips.label: Pearlescent wing sheen
idTips.description: Wings have a distinctive lustrous, pearl-like quality that shimmers when light hits them at different angles, almost like soap bubbles

idTips.label: Wing span size
idTips.description: Medium-sized moth with wings spanning roughly the width of a large coin (about 1-1.4 inches across)

idTips.label: Flight period
idTips.description: Adults are active from late spring through summer (May to August), flying primarily at night

idTips.label: Body structure
idTips.description: Typical moth body with feathery antennae and fuzzy thorax, wings held horizontally when at rest

idTips.label: Light attraction
idTips.description: Readily comes to porch lights and outdoor lighting, often found resting on nearby walls or surfaces in early morning

habitat: Pearly Wood-nymphs inhabit areas where their host plants thrive, including woodland edges, wetland margins, gardens, and disturbed areas. Look for them near wild grapes, evening primrose, hibiscus, and various wetland plants like swamp loosestrife. They're adaptable and can be found from forest clearings to suburban gardens throughout New England's lower elevations.

seasonality.spring: Late spring (May) marks the beginning of adult flight season. Look for fresh moths at lights during warm evenings.
seasonality.summer: Peak activity occurs through summer months (June-August). Adults are most commonly encountered at this time, attracted to outdoor lighting and feeding on flower nectar.
seasonality.fall: Adult activity winds down by late summer. Early fall may show worn individuals from the season's final generation.
seasonality.winter: No adult activity. The species overwinters in an immature stage, likely as pupae in the soil or leaf litter.

funFact: The caterpillars of Pearly Wood-nymphs are incredibly versatile eaters, munching on everything from wild grapes to hibiscus flowers to evening primrose — a diet so varied it spans completely different plant families, making them botanical omnivores of the insect world!
confusionNotes: Most likely confused with its close relative, the Beautiful Wood-nymph, which shares similar size and habits. The Beautiful Wood-nymph typically has more distinct wing patterns and coloration, while the Pearly Wood-nymph's defining feature is its characteristic lustrous sheen. When in doubt, focus on that telltale pearlescent quality of the wings.
contextualKnowledge: Despite the ethereal 'wood-nymph' name suggesting a purely forest-dwelling creature, these moths are quite adaptable and thrive in human-modified landscapes. The 'wood-nymph' name is more about their graceful, fairy-like flight pattern than their strict habitat preferences.
compareHints: The Pearly Wood-nymph differs from its genus mate, the Beautiful Wood-nymph, primarily in wing coloration and sheen. While the Beautiful Wood-nymph displays more contrasting patterns and colors, the Pearly Wood-nymph is distinguished by its namesake lustrous, pearl-like wing surface. Both species are similar in size and flight period, but the Pearly Wood-nymph's iridescent quality makes it relatively distinctive once you know what to look for.

relatedSpecies.distinction: The Beautiful Wood-nymph differs from its close relative, the Pearly Wood-nymph, primarily in its bird dropping camouflage colors - the Beautiful has more brown and tan tones mixed with white, while the Pearly is more stark black and white.
